Bumps [concurrently](https://github.com/open-cli-tools/concurrently) from 8.0.1 to 9.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from concurrently's releases.

v9.1.0

What's Changed

  • Remove signal event listeners on finish by @​gustavohenke in open-cli-tools/concurrently#512
  • Add support for Deno shortcuts and wildcards by @​mahtaran in open-cli-tools/concurrently#508
  • bin: show help when no args are passed by @​gustavohenke in open-cli-tools/concurrently#513

New Contributors

  • @​mahtaran made their first contribution in open-cli-tools/concurrently#508

Full Changelog: https://github.com/open-cli-tools/concurrently/compare/v9.0.1...v9.1.0

v9.0.1

What's Changed

  • Don't set up more than 1 abort signal listener by @​gustavohenke in open-cli-tools/concurrently#503

Full Changelog: https://github.com/open-cli-tools/concurrently/compare/v9.0.0...v9.0.1

v9.0.0

💥 Breaking Changes

  • Dropped support for Node.js < 18.0.0. Older Node.js version have reached end-of-life, and certain features require new-ish JS APIs.

  • The concurrently and default exports are now the same - #399 It's reasonable to expect that import { concurrently } from 'concurrently' would work the same as import concurrently from 'concurrently', however this has not been the case. The former used to be an unconfigured version of concurrently, lacking all features that you'd get from the CLI, which was seen as a "footgun". Both are now the same function.

    If you'd like to access the unconfigured function, use import { createConcurrently } from 'concurrently' instead.

✨ New Features

  • Exponential back-off support for process restarting - #265, #462 Use --restart-after exponential. Restarts happen at 2^N seconds.
  • Add prefix padding via new --pad-prefix flag - #166, #417, #495
  • Specify teardown commands via new --teardown flag - #472, #500
  • Expand node:<script> commands to node --run <script> - #475
  • [API only] Inter-Process Communication (ipc) - #498
  • [API only] Make it possible to use no colors at all - #466
  • [API only] Add a state field to Command - #455

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Fix importing concurrently in ESM package - #454, #456, #494
  • Make sure concurrently doesn't resolve when manually restarting commands through API - #463, #464
  • Abort commands not running when max processes < N - #433, #452, #460
  • Fix warning coming from spawn-command when running in Node 22 - #407, #477, #479, #492
  • Make --raw and --hide compatible - #394, #486
  • Ensure prefix is written when logging without a trailing LF - #467

Other Changes

  • --help no longer shows examples due to there being too many. Refer to https://github.com/open-cli-tools/concurrently/tree/v9.0.0/docs instead, or to the node_modules/concurrently/docs directory in your project.
  • Improve examples of --passthrough-arguments - #490

# Code Review: ZLMediaKit SrtCaller.cpp

## Summary

This review assesses the `SrtCaller.cpp` file, a new addition to the ZLMediaKit project. The file implements an SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) caller for media streaming.  The review focuses on code structure, readability, error handling, and potential performance improvements.

## Detailed Feedback

### Code Overview

`SrtCaller.cpp` implements a client-side SRT connection. It handles the SRT handshake, data transmission, and various control packets (ACK, NAK, KeepAlive, etc.).  The code uses a state machine-like approach to manage the connection lifecycle.

### Strengths

- **Comprehensive SRT Implementation:** The code appears to implement a fairly complete SRT client, handling various aspects of the protocol.
- **Modular Design:** The code is broken down into reasonably well-defined functions, improving readability and maintainability.
- **Error Handling (Partial):** Some error handling is present, particularly in `onResult`.
- **Use of Smart Pointers:**  The use of `std::shared_ptr` and `std::weak_ptr` helps manage object lifetimes effectively.
- **Configuration:** The code uses configuration parameters for various settings (latency, buffer size, timeout).


### Areas for Improvement

#### 1. Error Handling

- **Issue:** Error handling is inconsistent. While `onResult` handles some exceptions, many functions lack robust error checking.  For instance, functions like `sendPacket` and `sendDataPacket` don't check for potential errors from the underlying socket operations.  Failure to send a packet could lead to silent data loss.
- **Suggestion:** Add comprehensive error checking to all functions that interact with the socket or SRT protocol.  Log errors appropriately and consider using exceptions for critical errors.  Return error codes or status values to indicate success or failure.
- **Example:**

```cpp
void SrtCaller::sendPacket(Buffer::Ptr pkt, bool flush) {
    auto tmp = _packet_pool.obtain2();
    tmp->assign(pkt->data(), pkt->size());
    auto ret = _socket->send(std::move(tmp), nullptr, 0, flush); // Add error check here
    if (ret < 0) {
        ErrL << "Failed to send packet: " << ret << ", errno: " << errno;
        // Handle the error appropriately (e.g., retry, disconnect)
    }
    _send_ticker.resetTime();
    return;
}
```

#### 2. Logging

- **Issue:** The logging is inconsistent and sometimes insufficient.  `InfoL`, `DebugL`, `TraceL`, `WarnL`, and `ErrL` are used, but the level of detail and frequency of logging could be improved.  In some cases, important events might not be logged, making debugging difficult.
- **Suggestion:**  Establish a clear logging strategy.  Use more informative log messages, including relevant context (e.g., packet sequence numbers, timestamps).  Consider using a more structured logging system for better analysis.

#### 3.  Code Clarity and Readability

- **Issue:** Some parts of the code are difficult to follow, especially the packet handling and state machine logic.  Long functions like `inputSockData` could be broken down into smaller, more focused functions.  Meaningful variable names are crucial for understanding the code's purpose.
- **Suggestion:** Refactor the code to improve readability.  Break down large functions into smaller, more manageable units.  Use more descriptive variable names.  Add comments to explain complex logic.

#### 4.  Potential Performance Issues

- **Issue:** The `checkAndSendAckNak` function might be a performance bottleneck, especially under high load.  The repeated checks and conditional logic could introduce overhead.
- **Suggestion:** Consider optimizing `checkAndSendAckNak`.  Explore using timers or asynchronous operations to reduce the frequency of checks.

#### 5.  Security

- **Issue:** The code handles encryption, but the security aspects need a more thorough review.  The key management and encryption/decryption processes should be carefully examined for potential vulnerabilities.
- **Suggestion:** Conduct a security audit of the encryption and key management mechanisms.  Ensure that the chosen encryption algorithms are strong and up-to-date.  Follow secure coding practices to prevent vulnerabilities.


## Conclusion

`SrtCaller.cpp` provides a functional SRT client implementation, but improvements are needed in error handling, logging, code clarity, and performance.  A thorough security review is also recommended. Addressing these issues will significantly enhance the code's robustness, maintainability, and security.

작업 날 기준 구현되어진 모든 뷰를 연결하는 작업입니다.

## 4️⃣ 스크린샷
| ![newUserStart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a3f3271-49aa-4d12-8c44-748ab71cbd21) | ![GameStart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3878ff6b-f52b-4107-8e4c-6e6821f75012) | ![stageClear](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8855bf54-d3c7-451a-a12a-665733543cd2) |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **신규 유저 진입 화면** | **게임 플레이 화면(1~2단계)** | **3단계 및 캐릭터 해금 화면**


## 5️⃣ 체크리스트
- [x] 작성한 코드가 정상적으로 동작하나요?
- [x] 사전에 정해진 컨벤션을 지켜서 코드를 작성했나요?
- [x] Pull Request를 보내기 전 리뷰어와 할당자를 설정했나요?
- [x] 관련 이슈 번호를 작성했나요?

## 6️⃣ 리뷰 요구사항 및 추가 설명
### 진입부 코드 구현에 대해
진입부 EntryView를 새로 만들었습니다.
UUID가 있다면, 목데이터를 쓰도록 했습니다. 목데이터 위치는 `Sources/Presentation/Common/Mock/MockData.swift` 입니다.

즉 첫 실행시에는 온보딩으로 진입합니다. 그 이후에는 목데이터를 사용하게 됩니다. 목데이터는 실제 서버 연동시 추가하면 될 것 같아요.
삭제시 닉네임 변경으로 진입 가능합니다. 테스트 할 시, `Sources/App/AppEntryView.swift`에서 분기처리를 MainView 주석 후 OnboardingView로 바꿔주시면 됩니다.

### 일부 수정이 필요한 코드
1. 닉네임을 5글자로 하면 메인뷰에서 좌측 상단 카드 텍스트 길이가 안맞는 문제가 있었습니다. 이슈 만들어서 해야할 듯 해요.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/051c437a-95c7-4b71-9755-2a6c1447ba64)

2. 맵 뷰에서 유저의 스테이지 값에 따라 구역을 lock 해야 합니다. 지금은 스테이지가 1이어도 다른 구역을 다 터치할 수 있네요! 그 부분은 건드리지않았습니다. garden맵만 적용되어있어요.

### 수정한 코드
코드 최대한 안건드리려고 했는데 아래 부분은 통일이 필요할 것 같아서 수정했습니다.
스테이지가 클리어한 스테이지로 되어있어서 다른 코드와 조금 달랐어요! 
그래서 UserData에서 의미하는 stage는 현재 도전하는 스테이지로 통일했습니다. 즉, stage 2면, 2까지만 해금되어있는 걸로!

```swift
ImageMapButtonView(
    shape: shape,
    stageName: stageName,
    color: color,
    // 기존 로직 - stage가 클리어한 스테이지
    // isOpen: userData.stage >= stage.index,
    // isActive: userData.stage + 1 == stage.index
                        
    // 변경 로직 - stage가 현재 도전하는 스테이지
    isOpen: userViewModel.userData.stage > stage.index,
    isActive: userViewModel.userData.stage == stage.index
)
```

pull_request.body:
Solution for Day8.

In the first part a network of nodes is traversed from a start node to an end node with a given path. The steps to reach the final node are counted and this number gives the solution.

The second part complicates this significantly by requiring to start from six nodes using the same path at the same time where each of those node needs a different amount of steps to reach an end node. Thus, getting to a state where all nodes are end nodes requires many cycles of the same path and trillions of steps. This means any iterative/brute force attempt to solve the puzzle takes forever and a more straightforward way to solve the problem is to first calculate the amount of steps for each start node and then find the LCM (Least Common Multiple).

General Overview:

- "aoc8.py" is the entry point that prints the solutions for part one and two.
- "Network" class contains all the required methods to solve the puzzle (including technically correct but super inefficient iterative brute force methods)
- "Counter" is a new utility helper to pass a mutable counter
- "benchmark_helper" provides benchmark printouts for function runtime

>**Battery charge limiter is not working**
> It could be that Asus services are overwriting this limit after. You can stop them from Extra settings by clicking Stop button. Some models support only 80% limit, so try to set exactly 80% to be sure.

> After restart, BIOS resets all settings to defaults, including charge limit. As soon as you log in and G-Helper starts it would apply charge limit again. Before app starting - your laptop may keep charging. This is normal and this is how things are.

01/01/2025 10:50:39 pm: Optimization service is running

I see that you use `Ambient` backlight, that by definition changes color based on screen contents. Just change mode to anything else - and you will be fine.
